Node.js 27 arrives with a surprising shift: the default V8 heap limit is now 4 GB on machines with 8 GB of RAM, doubling the previous default.

The release adds lazy iterator helpers—Iterator.zip() and Iterator.zipKeyed()—that combine sequences without materialising intermediate arrays, and Math.sumPrecise() delivers exact numeric totals, removing floating‑point rounding errors.

Other notable changes include the upgrade to V8 15.6, the unflagged node:vfs module, and the new promises‑based net API. The runtime also moves to OpenSSL 4.1 and raises the default heap limit, while the permission model gains the --allow‑env flag.

"The new iterator helpers let pipelines stay memory‑efficient even with millions of items."  

These updates mean developers can write more memory‑friendly code, trust numeric aggregations, and benefit from a faster, more secure runtime out of the box.

The larger heap does not eliminate the need for proper back‑pressure or container‑level memory limits.
